flagged.evidence: The Statement defines “the observed treatment-stratum law P_a(C)=P(C∩{A=a})/P(A=a),” and the proof uses P_a for full-data expectations involving Y^a. Proof 5.1 then says, “Equal observed-data laws give the same P_L, stratum laws P_a, and P_a conditional-mean classes.” Equality of the observed (A,L,Y) law does not imply equality of these full conditional measures P_a: for example, with L constant and A independent of the potential outcomes, two models can have the same Bernoulli(1/2) observed Y in both treatment arms but different couplings of (Y^0,Y^1). The identifiability conclusion follows from equality of the (L,Y) marginals of P_a, but that restriction is not stated here.
